title: Stewed chicken with tomato-based sauce, Mexican style

content.title: About
content.content: Stewed chicken in a Mexican‑style tomato sauce is made from bite‑size pieces of chicken breast or thigh, slowly simmered in a fragrant blend of tomatoes, chilies, onion, garlic and spices (cumin, oregano, coriander). The dish has a rich, mildly spicy flavor with a hint of acidity and the characteristic aroma of Mexican cuisine.

content.title: Interesting Facts
items: Mexican tomato sauces often include fresh chilies, giving the dish its signature heat.
Chicken is traditionally marinated in lime juice before cooking to keep the meat tender.
The stew is commonly served with corn tortillas, rice, or beans.
Mexican cooking relies heavily on aromatic herbs and spices such as cumin and coriander to boost flavor.
Slow‑cooking helps retain most of the nutrients in both the meat and the sauce.

items.title: High‑quality protein
items.content: Chicken provides complete protein essential for muscle growth and tissue repair.

items.title: B‑vitamins
items.content: Chicken contains B3 (niacin) and B6, which support energy metabolism and nervous system function.

items.title: Lycopene in tomatoes
items.content: Tomatoes are rich in lycopene, an antioxidant that may help protect cells from oxidative damage.

items.title: Beneficial minerals
items.content: The dish supplies potassium, magnesium and iron, important for muscle function and blood health.

items.title: Low in saturated fat
items.content: When prepared with skinless chicken and minimal oil, the stew remains relatively low‑calorie.

items.title: Spice level
items.content: The chilies can be too hot for people with sensitive stomachs or gastritis.

items.title: Chicken allergy
items.content: Some individuals may experience allergic reactions to chicken.

items.title: Sodium content
items.content: Using canned tomato paste or broth can raise the sodium level of the sauce.

items.title: Undercooking risk
items.content: Chicken should reach an internal temperature of 75 °C to prevent salmonella.

content.title: How to Eat
content.content: Serve the stew hot, typically with corn or flour tortillas, rice, beans, or a fresh salad. Optional toppings include avocado, sour cream, or shredded cheese for a milder taste.

content.title: Storage
content.content: Keep leftovers in an airtight container in the refrigerator for up to 3‑4 days. For longer storage, freeze for up to 2 months after cooling to room temperature.
